title: Keep Multiplying Found Values by Two
summary: Given an array of integers and an initial value, repeatedly multiply the value by two if found in the array until the value is no longer present.
statement: Given an array of integers and an initial value, repeatedly multiply the value by two if found in the array until the value is no longer present.
constraints: nums contains positive integers and original is positive.
While the current value appears anywhere in nums, double it; array elements are not consumed.
Return the first resulting value absent from nums.
reference_solution:
def final_doubled_value(nums,original):
    values=set(nums)
    while original in values:original*=2
    return original

hints: Membership does not consume occurrences, so a set is the exact needed structure.
Repeatedly test current value and multiply by two while found.
Build values=set(nums); while original in values: original*=2; return original.
The loop follows the mandated deterministic sequence and stops precisely at its first absent value.

tests.explanation: Three, six, and twelve appear successively, so doubling stops at twenty-four.
Four is absent initially, so it is returned unchanged.
